questions.prompt: A team scales all features using statistics from the full dataset, then splits off the test set. What problem have they created?
options: Underfitting, because scaling removes useful detail
Data leakage, because test data shaped the training
High bias, because the model becomes too simple
No problem, because scaling does not change labels

questions.prompt: In a linear model of house price from square footage, training means searching for the slope and intercept that best match the data.
A music app has listening histories for millions of users but no tags or categories. It wants to find groups of users with similar tastes. Which type of learning fits, and why?
A model uses age, in years, and salary, in dollars, as features without scaling. What is the likely problem?
options: Age dominates because it changes more often
Salary dominates because its numbers are much larger
Both features are ignored by the model
The target becomes harder to define

questions.prompt: Adding more and more features always makes patterns easier to find, since the model has more information.
As you raise the polynomial order of a regression model, what happens to its bias and to its variance?
A data scientist checks the test set after every hyperparameter change and keeps whatever scores best. What is wrong with this, and what should she use instead?
During training, the error jumps around and never settles near a minimum. Which change is most likely to help?
options: Raise the learning rate to move faster
Add more epochs at the same settings
Lower the learning rate to take smaller steps
Remove momentum so steps stay steady
